_comment: Greptile review configuration. Ported from .coderabbit.yaml on 2026-07-31; CodeRabbit is paused (reviews.auto_review.enabled: false) but still installed, so switching back is one flag there and deleting this file here. NOTE: settings are read from the PR's SOURCE branch, so a change here takes effect on the PR that introduces it. If a .greptile/ directory ever appears it takes precedence and this file is ignored entirely.
_comment_strictness: 2 is the default. CodeRabbit ran on the `assertive` profile, but Greptile documents strictness only as a severity threshold without stating direction, so this starts neutral rather than guessing. Adjust after a few reviews.
_comment_triggers: Both false for the same reason auto_incremental_review was off in CodeRabbit: the review loop pushes fixes on nearly every PR, and re-reviewing each push burns the quota two or three times per PR. Redundant while skipReview is AUTOMATIC, kept explicit so re-enabling automatic reviews does not silently also re-enable per-push ones.
_comment_statusCheck: false — solo repo, reviews inform rather than gate merges (CodeRabbit's request_changes_workflow: false). Once a `main` ruleset exists it should require Quality Checks, Unit Tests, Python Checks, Build, Static Analysis and Playwright E2E; review bots are deliberately not among them.
_comment_ignorePatterns: Generated, vendored and lock artifacts. docs/session-metrics-reports/** and docs/current-state.md are generated or overwritten each session by the /wrap skill. Do NOT add `docs/**`: a docs-titled PR in the predecessor repo turned out to carry a real data-loss bug, and the review is what caught it.
ignorePatterns:
**/*.lock
pnpm-lock.yaml
node_modules/**
.next/**
dist/**
.venv/**
supabase/**/generated/**
docs/session-metrics-reports/**
docs/current-state.md

rules.rule: Grounding and authorship guardrails. Flag any change that could drop a required per-fact citation, surface an art-historical claim not grounded in a retrieved source (confabulation), or introduce a path that generates imagery rather than analysing work the artist supplied.
Zod contracts must stay in sync with the Python Pydantic models in artloupe-schemas. Flag drift between the two.

Accessibility must meet WCAG 2.2 AA and ARIA authoring practices. Flag missing or incorrect semantic HTML, non-text controls without accessible names, keyboard traps or unreachable interactive elements, focus not managed on dynamic UI (dialogs, route changes, live regions), colour used as the only signal or insufficient contrast, images and icons without text alternatives, form fields without associated labels or error messaging, and hard-coded user-facing copy that bypasses next-intl.
